subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should OpenClaw make custom cron job IDs a supported public create-time CLI/Gateway/API contract, and if so what validation and collision behavior should that contract guarantee?
rationale: The implementation is technically bounded, but it changes a public cron creation/API surface and user-controlled identifier rules, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Approve a bounded custom-ID contract
options.body: Add optional safe custom IDs for cron creation with explicit validation, duplicate rejection, UUID default preservation, docs, and tests across CLI/Gateway/service callers.

options.title: Keep UUID-only creation
options.body: Reject the feature direction and close the request after documenting that users should rely on generated IDs plus list/search/display improvements.

options.title: Narrow to display improvements
options.body: Do not support create-time IDs yet, but improve list/show/UI discoverability through the related cron identifier display work.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded custom-ID contract
recommendation.body: Add optional safe custom IDs for cron creation with explicit validation, duplicate rejection, UUID default preservation, docs, and tests across CLI/Gateway/service callers.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history place him on the current cron CLI/type/schema/service surfaces where the public contract would be set.
